examples.ko: 선생님이 칠판에 대분수 문제를 내 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher put a mixed number problem on the board.
We learned how to change an improper fraction into a mixed number.
A number like 2 and 1/3 is called a mixed number.
When you add mixed numbers, you calculate the whole numbers first.
Shall we change this mixed number into an improper fraction?
My younger sibling says mixed number calculations are hard.

explain: 자연수와 분수가 함께 있는 수예요. '가분수'(분자가 분모보다 큰 분수)와 짝으로 자주 나오고, 2와 3분의 1처럼 '와'를 넣어 읽어요.
explain_en: It is a number made of a whole number plus a fraction. It often appears together with '가분수' (improper fraction), and you read 2⅓ as '2와 3분의 1', using '와'.

examples.ko: 바람이 불자 대숲에서 사각사각 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When the wind blew, a rustling sound came from the bamboo grove.
There is a big bamboo grove behind the village.

examples.ko: 대숲 사이로 난 길을 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly along the path through the bamboo grove.
It is cool inside the bamboo grove even in summer.

examples.ko: 우리는 대숲 길을 따라 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: We took photos along the bamboo grove path.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날의 대숲은 더 조용해요.
examples.en: The bamboo grove is even quieter on a rainy day.

explain: 대나무가 모여 자라는 숲이에요. '대나무 숲'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 하고, 글이나 노래에서는 바람 소리와 함께 자주 나와요. 받침 'ㅍ' 때문에 [대숩]으로 발음해요.
explain_en: It is a forest where bamboo grows together. People also say it in full as '대나무 숲', and it often appears in writing and songs together with the sound of wind. Because of the final 'ㅍ', it is pronounced [대숩].

examples.en: I borrowed comic books from the neighborhood rental shop.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞에 비디오 대여점이 있었어요.
examples.en: There used to be a video rental shop in front of my house.

examples.ko: 캠핑 장비는 대여점에 가면 싸게 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can rent camping gear cheaply if you go to a rental shop.
This rental shop is closed on Sundays.
There are many hanbok rental shops near tourist spots.
The owner of the rental shop recommended a book to me.

explain: 물건을 빌려주는 가게예요. 앞에 '만화책, 비디오, 한복, 캠핑 장비'처럼 빌려주는 물건을 붙여서 말해요. 요즘은 '렌탈샵'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a shop that lends things out. You put the item before it, like '만화책, 비디오, 한복, 캠핑 장비'. These days people also say '렌탈샵'.

examples.en: I was away from home for five or six days because of a business trip.
It took about five or six days for my cold to get better.
I will contact you again in five or six days.

examples.ko: 이 김치는 대엿새 정도 두면 맛이 들어요.
examples.en: This kimchi gets good flavor if you leave it for five or six days.
There are only five or six days of vacation left.
I need five or six days to prepare for the trip.

explain: 닷새나 엿새쯤, 대략 5~6일을 말해요. 같은 식으로 3~4일은 '사나흘'이라고 해요. 발음은 [대엳쌔]예요.
explain_en: It means roughly five or six days. In the same way, three or four days is '사나흘'. It is pronounced [대엳쌔].

examples.en: The company considers its external image important.
My outside activities have increased, so I am very busy.

examples.ko: 이 소식은 대외적 발표 전까지 비밀이에요.
examples.en: This news is a secret until the public announcement.
On the outside, there seems to be no particular problem.
That country has high credibility abroad.
The CEO is in charge of external matters.

explain: 안쪽(내부)이 아니라 바깥, 곧 다른 나라나 외부 사람을 상대하는 것을 말해요. 반대말은 '대내적'이고, '대외적으로'처럼 쓰는 일이 많아요. 뉴스나 회사 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is about dealing with the outside, such as other countries or outside people, rather than the inside. Its opposite is '대내적', and it is often used as '대외적으로'. You will hear it in news and talk about companies.

examples.en: I used olive oil as a substitute for butter.
This is not the real thing; it is a substitute.

examples.ko: 설탕 대용품을 사 봤는데 맛이 달라요.
examples.en: I tried a sugar substitute, but the taste is different.

examples.ko: 급할 때 쓸 대용품이 하나 있으면 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to have a substitute you can use in a hurry.
They say this powder is a milk substitute.

examples.ko: 비싼 걸 살 수 없으면 대용품이라도 쓸 만해요.
examples.en: If you can't buy the expensive one, even a substitute is good enough.

explain: 원래 쓰려던 물건 대신 쓰는 물건이에요. '버터 대용품'처럼 '무엇의 대용품' 형태로 말해요. 진짜보다 조금 못하다는 느낌이 있어서 '대체품'보다 아쉬운 뉘앙스가 날 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a thing used in place of what you originally meant to use, in the form '무엇의 대용품' like '버터 대용품'. It can carry a slight feeling of being a bit inferior to the real thing, so it may sound more disappointing than '대체품'.

examples.en: The flu spreads widely every winter.
This song was a huge hit last year.

examples.ko: 요즘 이 게임이 대유행이라서 다들 해요.
examples.en: This game is a huge craze these days, so everyone plays it.
The school closed because of the outbreak.
That hairstyle was a huge fad for a while.
A worldwide outbreak has begun.

explain: 그냥 '유행'보다 훨씬 크게 퍼진다는 느낌이에요. 노래나 옷 같은 유행에도 쓰고, 병이 크게 퍼질 때도 써요. 보통 '대유행이다, 대유행을 하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It feels much bigger than plain '유행' (trend). You can use it for trends like songs and clothes, and also when a disease spreads widely. It is usually said as '대유행이다' or '대유행을 하다'.

examples.en: For a while, this song was a huge hit across the country.
Long padded coats were all the rage last winter.
This dance is hugely popular on social media.
It looks like the flu will spread widely this year.

examples.ko: 내가 학교 다닐 때 이 게임이 대유행했거든요.
examples.en: This game was a huge craze when I was in school.
What kind of clothes are all the rage these days?

explain: '유행하다'보다 크게 퍼졌다는 뜻을 더해요. 같은 뜻으로 '크게 유행하다'라고도 말해요. 노래, 옷, 게임뿐 아니라 병이 퍼질 때도 써요.
explain_en: It adds the sense of spreading much more widely than '유행하다'. You can also say '크게 유행하다' for the same meaning. It is used for songs, clothes and games, and also when a disease spreads.

examples.en: The government came up with a new countermeasure.

examples.ko: 이번 사고에 대한 대응책 마련이 시급해요.
examples.en: Preparing a response to this accident is urgent.
I can't think of a good countermeasure.
What are you thinking of as a countermeasure?

examples.ko: 이 대응책은 비용이 너무 많이 들어요.
examples.en: This countermeasure costs too much.

examples.ko: 미리 대응책을 알아 두면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: If you know the countermeasures in advance, you feel at ease.

explain: '대책'이라고도 해요. 보통 '대응책을 세우다/마련하다/내놓다'처럼 써요. 문제나 상대의 움직임에 맞서서 하는 방법이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: People also say '대책'. It is usually used as '대응책을 세우다/마련하다/내놓다'. It carries the feeling of a method to face a problem or another party's actions.

examples.en: While traveling, I felt the beauty of nature.
In front of grand nature, people look small.
I want to rest for a few days in the great outdoors.
This movie was shot against a backdrop of vast nature.
Feel the peace that nature gives.
We are a part of nature.

explain: 그냥 '자연'보다 크고 웅장한 느낌이에요. 산, 바다, 사막처럼 넓은 자연을 말할 때 어울려요. 말할 때보다 글이나 여행 이야기에서 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It feels bigger and more majestic than plain '자연'. It suits wide landscapes such as mountains, seas and deserts. It fits writing and travel stories better than casual talk.

en: big party; big festival; big feast

examples.en: A big food festival was held in our neighborhood.
They say the supermarket is having a big sale today.
The school festival is a big celebration for the students.

examples.ko: 명절에 온 가족이 모여 먹고 마시는 대잔치가 벌어졌어요.
examples.en: At the holiday, the whole family gathered for a big feast.
Would you like to go to the spring festival?
During the big sale, prices go down a lot.

explain: 큰 잔치라는 뜻인데, 실제로는 '할인 대잔치, 먹거리 대잔치'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여 행사 이름이나 광고 문구로 많이 써요. 가게 간판이나 전단에서 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means a big party, but in practice you attach a word before it, like '할인 대잔치' or '먹거리 대잔치', as an event name or ad phrase. You can see it on shop signs and flyers.

examples.en: We chartered a bus for the group trip.

examples.ko: 하루 동안 택시를 대절하면 비용이 얼마예요?
examples.en: How much does it cost to charter a taxi for a day?
We chartered a tour bus and went on a picnic.

examples.ko: 대절한 버스가 아침 일곱 시에 출발해요.
examples.en: The chartered bus leaves at seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 결혼식에 갈 때 버스를 대절하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to charter a bus to go to the wedding.
You board the chartered bus in front of the school.

explain: 버스나 택시를 통째로 빌려 쓰는 일이에요. '버스 대절, 택시 대절'처럼 말하고, 보통 '대절하다'로 써요. 한 사람이 차를 빌려 직접 운전하는 렌터카와는 달라요.
explain_en: It means hiring a whole bus or taxi for your own use, as in '버스 대절' or '택시 대절', and it is usually used as '대절하다'. It differs from a rental car, which one person rents and drives.

examples.ko: 전기차 대중화를 위해서는 충전소가 더 늘어나야 해요.
examples.en: For electric cars to become common, there need to be more charging stations.

examples.ko: 인터넷의 대중화로 누구나 쉽게 정보를 찾을 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: With the spread of the internet, anyone can now find information easily.

examples.ko: 이 기술을 대중화하려면 값이 싸져야 해요.
examples.en: To make this technology popular, the price has to come down.
Smartphones became widespread, and life became more convenient.
Yoga has become quite popular in Korea too.

examples.ko: 어떻게 하면 클래식을 대중화할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: How can we make classical music popular?

explain: 소수만 쓰던 것이 많은 사람이 쓰게 되는 것, 또는 그렇게 만드는 것을 말해요. '대중화(가) 되다'라고 말하기도 해요. 기술, 스포츠, 문화 이야기에서 잘 나와요.
explain_en: It is about something once used by only a few becoming used by many, or making that happen. People also say '대중화(가) 되다'. It often appears in talk about technology, sports and culture.

examples.en: The tournament bracket was announced today.
Looking at the bracket, our first opponent is a strong team.
When and how is the bracket drawn?

examples.ko: 우리 반 대진표에 내 이름이 있어요.
examples.en: My name is on our class's bracket.
According to the bracket, we meet in the final.
I took a photo of the bracket posted on the board.

explain: 누가 누구와 겨루는지 순서를 그려 놓은 표예요. 학교 체육대회, 스포츠 대회, 게임 대회에서 쓰고, '대진표를 짜다/뽑다/발표하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a chart that shows who plays whom and in what order. It is used for school sports days, sports tournaments and game tournaments, and you say '대진표를 짜다/뽑다/발표하다'.

examples.en: The general trend is not bad.
The test results were good on the whole.
The rough schedule has already been decided.
Just tell me the rough outline.
People's opinions were generally similar.
If the general direction is right, let's keep going.

explain: 세부가 아니라 전체의 큰 틀을 말할 때 써요. '대체로 좋아요'처럼 '대체로'로도 말하는데, '대체적으로'는 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it for the big picture rather than the details. People also say '대체로 좋아요' with '대체로', while '대체적으로' feels a little more like written language.

examples.en: There is a jujube tree in the yard of my grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 대추나무에 열매가 빨갛게 익어요.
examples.en: In autumn, the fruit on the jujube tree ripens red.
Children are playing under the jujube tree.

examples.ko: 이 대추나무는 올해 열매가 많이 열렸어요.
examples.en: This jujube tree bore a lot of fruit this year.
We planted a jujube tree in the yard.

examples.ko: 대추나무 가지에 가시가 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The jujube tree's branches have thorns, so you have to be careful.

explain: 대추가 열리는 나무예요. 대추는 차나 한방 재료, 명절 음식에 많이 써요. 옛날이야기나 속담에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 그는 대추나무 연 걸리듯 빚이 여기저기 있어요.
phrases.en: He has debts here and there, like kites hanging all over a jujube tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빚이 여기저기 많이 걸려 있는 모양을 말해요. 가지에 연이 잔뜩 걸린 모습에 빗댄 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone with debts scattered everywhere, comparing it to kites snagged all over the branches.
phrases.en_equiv: be up to one's neck in debt

explain_en: It is the tree that bears jujubes. Jujubes are widely used in tea, herbal medicine and holiday food. The tree also appears in old tales and proverbs.

examples.en: I made a library card at the library.

examples.ko: 대출증이 없으면 책을 빌릴 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't borrow books without a library card.

examples.ko: 대출증은 신분증만 있으면 바로 만들어 줘요.
examples.en: They make a library card on the spot if you have an ID.
Please enter your library card number.
I'd like to make a card for my child too.
I lost my library card, so I applied for a replacement.

explain: 도서관에서 책을 빌릴 때 쓰는 카드예요. '대출'은 은행 대출도 되지만, '대출증'은 보통 도서관 카드로 이해하면 돼요. '회원증'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is the card you use to borrow books at a library. '대출' can also mean a bank loan, but '대출증' is usually understood as a library card. People also say '회원증' (membership card).

examples.en: The government announced a substantial reduction.
They are holding a sale with big discounts.
This year the budget increased substantially.
They say the company is making a major reorganization.
I was surprised because prices rose sharply.

examples.ko: 대폭적인 지원 덕분에 학교가 새로 지어졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the generous support, the school was newly built.

explain: 늘거나 줄거나 바뀌는 폭이 아주 클 때 써요. '인상, 인하, 할인, 개편, 증가'와 자주 같이 나와요. 짧게 부사 '대폭'을 써서 '대폭 줄었어요'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when an increase, decrease or change is very large. It often goes with '인상, 인하, 할인, 개편, 증가'. You can also use the short adverb '대폭', as in '대폭 줄었어요'.

examples.ko: 연착 안내 방송이 나오자 대합실이 술렁였어요.
examples.en: When the announcement about the delay came, the waiting room stirred.

examples.ko: 아이는 대합실에서 어머니를 찾자마자 울음을 터트렸어요.
examples.en: The child burst into tears as soon as he found his mother in the waiting room.

examples.ko: 대합실에 사람이 많아서 앉을 자리가 없어요.
examples.en: There are so many people in the waiting room that there is no seat.

examples.ko: 버스 터미널 대합실은 난방이 잘돼서 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The bus terminal waiting room is well heated, so it is warm.
I sat on a chair in the waiting room and read a book.
I went out to the station waiting room to meet my friend.

explain: 기차역이나 버스 터미널에서 차를 기다리는 곳이에요. 병원에서 기다리는 곳은 보통 '대기실'이라고 해요. 발음은 [대합씰]이에요.
explain_en: It is the place to wait for a train or bus at a station or terminal. The waiting area at a hospital is usually called '대기실'. It is pronounced [대합씰].

examples.en: When the power went out, the subway station fell into chaos.
The roads are in chaos because of the sudden snow.
The exam schedule changed, and great confusion broke out.
Right after the accident, the scene was total chaos.
I acted calmly even in the midst of the chaos.
The server stopped, and the reservations went into chaos.

explain: '혼란'보다 훨씬 크고 정신없는 상태예요. 보통 '대혼란에 빠지다, 대혼란이 일어나다, 대혼란을 겪다'로 써요. 반대로 질서가 있는 상태는 '질서'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a much bigger, more frantic state than '혼란'. It is usually used as '대혼란에 빠지다, 대혼란이 일어나다, 대혼란을 겪다'. The opposite state, with things in order, is '질서'.

examples.en: Great floods often appear in old tales.
Last summer, the village was flooded by a great flood.

examples.ko: 대홍수 때문에 많은 사람이 집을 떠났어요.
examples.en: Many people left their homes because of the great flood.
I saw news about the great flood on TV.

examples.ko: 그 강은 대홍수를 몇 번 겪었어요.
examples.en: That river has been through great floods several times.

examples.ko: 대홍수 뒤에 복구 작업이 한참 이어졌어요.
examples.en: After the great flood, the recovery work went on for a long time.

explain: '홍수'보다 규모가 아주 큰 홍수예요. 뉴스, 옛이야기, 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 평소 비가 많이 와서 길이 잠기는 정도는 그냥 '홍수'나 '침수'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a flood on a much larger scale than '홍수'. It often appears in news, old tales and history. When heavy rain just floods roads, people usually say plain '홍수' or '침수'.

examples.en: It's cold, and on top of that, the wind is blowing too.

examples.ko: 몸도 안 좋은데 더더구나 일까지 많아요.
examples.en: I don't feel well, and on top of that I have a lot of work.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 비싸고 더더구나 색도 마음에 안 들어요.
examples.en: This outfit is expensive, and moreover I don't even like the color.

examples.ko: 저는 요리를 못하는데 더더구나 오늘은 재료도 없어요.
examples.en: I'm bad at cooking, and what's more, I have no ingredients today.

examples.ko: 길도 막히고 더더구나 비까지 와서 늦었어요.
examples.en: The roads were jammed, and on top of that it rained, so I was late.

examples.ko: 더더구나 이렇게 늦은 시간에는 갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Especially at such a late hour, I can't go.

explain: '더구나'를 더 힘주어 말하는 느낌이에요. 앞의 이야기에 더해서 상황이 더 심해지거나 더 그렇다는 걸 덧붙일 때 써요. 말할 때는 '게다가'나 '더구나'로 바꿔도 돼요.
explain_en: It feels like a more emphatic version of '더구나'. Use it to add that, on top of what you just said, the situation is even more so. In speech you can swap it for '게다가' or '더구나'.

examples.en: With the rain, it became even colder.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 들으니 더한층 열심히 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: Hearing praise makes me want to work even harder.

examples.ko: 이야기를 들을수록 그 사람이 더한층 궁금해요.
examples.en: The more I hear the story, the more curious I am about that person.
As the exam got closer, my nervousness grew even more.

examples.ko: 도움을 받은 뒤로 그에게 더한층 고마운 마음이 생겼어요.
examples.en: After receiving his help, I felt even more grateful to him.

examples.ko: 밤이 깊어 갈수록 바람이 더한층 거세졌어요.
examples.en: As the night deepened, the wind grew even stronger.

explain: 이미 어느 정도인 상태가 한 단계 더 심해질 때 써요. 말할 때는 '더욱'이나 '훨씬 더'를 더 자주 쓰는 편이고, '더한층'은 글에서 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when a state that is already somewhat so goes one level further. In speech, '더욱' or '훨씬 더' can replace it, and '더한층' suits writing better.

examples.en: The children are playing a ball-throwing game.

examples.ko: 오늘 체육 시간에 멀리 던지기를 했어요.
examples.en: In PE class today, we did a long-distance throw.

examples.ko: 눈덩이 던지기는 겨울에만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only throw snowballs in winter.
I want to become a discus thrower.

examples.ko: 던지기 연습을 매일 했더니 실력이 늘었어요.
examples.en: I practiced throwing every day, and my skill improved.
I won a doll at the ring toss game.

explain: 단독으로는 잘 안 쓰고 '공 던지기, 고리 던지기, 돌 던지기'처럼 던지는 물건을 앞에 붙여요. 육상 종목은 '원반던지기, 창던지기'처럼 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is not used much alone; you put the thrown object before it, as in '공 던지기, 고리 던지기, 돌 던지기'. Track and field events are often written together, like '원반던지기' and '창던지기'.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my body is shivering.
My hands trembled with fear.

examples.ko: 겨울 바람 속에서 덜덜 떨며 버스를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited for the bus, shivering in the winter wind.

examples.ko: 시험 전에는 다리가 덜덜 떨릴 만큼 긴장돼요.
examples.en: Before the exam, I'm so nervous that my legs shake.

examples.ko: 낡은 세탁기가 덜덜 소리를 내며 돌아가요.
examples.en: The old washing machine runs with a rattling noise.
He spoke while trembling.

explain: 추위나 무서움 때문에 몸이 크게 떨리는 모양이에요. 보통 '덜덜 떨다, 덜덜 떨리다'로 써요. '달달'은 더 작고 가볍게 떠는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes the body shaking hard from cold or fear, usually as '덜덜 떨다' or '덜덜 떨리다'. '달달' gives a smaller, lighter shaking feel.

examples.en: I was so cold that my jaw was chattering.
The old bus rattled as it set off.
The washing machine was rattling, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 그렇게 덜덜거리지 말고 숨을 크게 쉬어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't shake like that; try taking a deep breath.
The old window rattles in the wind all night.
I was so nervous that my hands shook.

explain: 사람이 떨 때도 쓰고, 기계나 창문이 흔들리며 소리 낼 때도 써요. '덜덜대다'라고도 말해요. 몸이 떨리는 일에는 '덜덜 떨다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a person shakes and also when a machine or window rattles. You can also say '덜덜대다'. For a shaking body, '덜덜 떨다' is used even more.

examples.en: He took the news of the breakup calmly.

examples.ko: 덤덤한 표정으로 이야기하니 더 슬프게 들렸어요.
examples.en: Because he talked with an expressionless face, it sounded even sadder.
Even after hearing I passed, I feel oddly calm.
As I got older, I became indifferent to small things.
Even when I praise him he stays unmoved, so I can't tell if he's happy.
The child stayed unfazed even after getting a shot.

explain: 기쁨이나 슬픔을 겉으로 크게 드러내지 않는 모습이에요. 보통 '무덤덤하다'로도 말해요. 음식이 밍밍해서 맛이 별로 없을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes someone who doesn't show joy or sadness outwardly. People often say '무덤덤하다' too. It can also be used for bland food that has little flavor.

examples.en: My younger sibling was careless and broke a cup.
Don't be careless; check slowly.
That's why you keep losing things when you're so careless.
The child came running down the stairs in a hurry.
My older brother is hasty by nature, so he makes many mistakes.
I want to fix my habit of being careless.

explain: 침착하지 못하고 서두르다가 실수하는 모습이에요. '덤벙대다'와 뜻이 같고, 비슷한 말로 '덜렁대다'가 있어요. 반대로 차분한 사람은 '침착하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes rushing without calm and making mistakes. It means the same as '덤벙대다', and a similar word is '덜렁대다'. A calm person is described as '침착하다'.

examples.en: Don't be careless; check your homework carefully.
He was careless and lost his keys.

examples.ko: 시험 볼 때 덤벙대서 쉬운 문제를 틀렸어요.
examples.en: I was careless during the test and got an easy question wrong.
Because I'm careless by nature, I always make mistakes.
The children came bursting into the classroom in a rush.

examples.ko: 친구가 덤벙대면 제가 옆에서 챙겨 줘요.
examples.en: When my friend is being careless, I look after things beside him.

explain: '덤벙거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 서두르거나 침착하지 못해서 실수하는 사람에게 써요. 비슷한 말로 '덜렁대다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '덤벙거리다'. It is used for someone who rushes or is not calm and makes mistakes. A similar word is '덜렁대다'.

examples.en: There are several dump trucks at the construction site.
A dump truck passed by, full of soil.
The child likes toy dump trucks.
I woke up because of the sound of a dump truck.

examples.ko: 덤프트럭은 짐칸을 들어 올려서 짐을 쏟아요.
examples.en: A dump truck raises its bed to unload its cargo.

examples.ko: 길에서 덤프트럭 뒤를 따라가면 먼지가 많아요.
examples.en: If you follow behind a dump truck on the road, there is a lot of dust.

explain: 흙이나 모래를 싣고 짐칸을 기울여 쏟는 트럭이에요. 영어 dump truck에서 온 말이고, 공사장에서 많이 봐요. 아이들 장난감이나 그림책에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a truck that carries soil or sand and tips its bed to unload. The word comes from the English 'dump truck', and you often see them at construction sites. It also appears in children's toys and picture books.

examples.en: My snaggletooth shows a little when I smile.
I had my crooked tooth corrected when I was young.

examples.ko: 친구는 덧니 때문에 웃는 모습이 귀여워요.
examples.en: My friend's smile is cute because of the snaggletooth.
My younger sibling has one snaggletooth.
They say straightening a crooked tooth takes a long time.
A snaggletooth is harder to brush than it looks.

explain: 가지런한 이 옆에 겹쳐서 난 이를 말해요. '덧니가 나다, 덧니가 있다'처럼 쓰고, 소리는 [던니]예요. 귀엽다고 매력 포인트로 말하는 사람도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a tooth that grows overlapping beside the neat row. It is used as '덧니가 나다' or '덧니가 있다' and sounds like [던니]. Some people see it as a cute, charming point.

examples.ko: 무릎 구멍 난 곳에 천을 덧댔어요.
examples.en: I patched the hole at the knee with a piece of cloth.
I put plastic over the window to keep out the cold.

examples.ko: 낡은 신발 밑창에 고무를 덧대서 신어요.
examples.en: I add rubber to the sole of my worn-out shoes and wear them.

examples.ko: 상처 위에 거즈를 덧대고 붕대를 감았어요.
examples.en: I laid gauze over the wound and wrapped a bandage.
Please put a wooden splint on the broken leg.
I came to buy cloth to patch jeans with.

explain: 구멍이나 약한 곳 위에 천, 판 같은 것을 한 겹 더 대는 거예요. '덧붙이다'는 말이나 내용을 더할 때 많이 쓰고, '덧대다'는 물건을 겉에 대는 데 써요.
explain_en: It means laying another layer, such as cloth or a board, over a hole or weak spot. '덧붙이다' is commonly used for adding words or content, while '덧대다' is for putting a physical item on the surface.

examples.en: The ball rolled down the hill.
The child is rolling around on the bed.

examples.ko: 배가 너무 아파서 바닥에서 데굴데굴 굴렀어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt so much that I rolled around on the floor.
The apples tumbled out of the bag, rolling.
The puppy is rolling around on the lawn.
It was so funny I almost rolled on the floor laughing.

explain: 둥글고 큰 것이 계속 구르는 모양이에요. 보통 '데굴데굴 구르다/굴러가다'로 써요. 더 센 느낌은 '떼굴떼굴', 작은 것에는 '대굴대굴'을 써요.
explain_en: It describes something round and fairly large rolling continuously, usually as '데굴데굴 구르다/굴러가다'. '떼굴떼굴' is a stronger version, and '대굴대굴' is used for smaller things.

examples.en: I put the screwdriver in the tool box.
I opened the tool box, and there was no hammer.

examples.ko: 도구함이 너무 무거워서 혼자 못 들겠어요.
examples.en: The tool box is so heavy that I can't lift it alone.
I should tidy up the tool box.
There is a small tool box in the car trunk.

examples.ko: 이 도구함에는 기본 공구가 다 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This tool box has all the basic tools in it.

explain: 공구나 도구를 넣어 두는 상자예요. 비슷한 말로 '공구함'이 있고, 옛날식으로 '연장통'이라고도 해요. 집에서는 못, 망치, 드라이버 같은 것을 넣어 두는 곳이에요.
explain_en: It is a box for keeping tools. Similar words are '공구함' and, in an older style, '연장통'. At home it holds things like nails, a hammer and a screwdriver.
